reason_summary: SegFormer-B2 achieves the highest weighted suitability score (8.55/10) for the FloodNet dataset. Its hierarchical Mix Transformer encoder captures both local texture (roads, buildings, vehicles) and global context (flood extent, water bodies) simultaneously. It requires fewer parameters than competitors while achieving state-of-the-art mIoU (~0.72) when fine-tuned on FloodNet per published IEEE benchmarks.

ranked_models.name: SegFormer-B2 (Mix Transformer)
strengths: Hierarchical Transformer encoder captures both local texture AND global context
Overlapping patch embeddings preserve spatial detail for roads/buildings
Mix-FFN uses depth-wise convolution — efficient for aerial image resolution
Lightweight all-MLP decoder reduces computation vs. complex heads
State-of-the-art on FloodNet (mIoU ~0.72 fine-tuned, per IEEE 2023 paper)
Efficient: 25M params — practical for inference on edge hardware
ADE20K pretrain includes water, road, building classes → strong transfer
weaknesses: Requires fine-tuning on FloodNet (zero-shot score is low without it)
Slightly more complex to train than U-Net

ranked_models.name: Mask2Former (Swin-T backbone)
strengths: Universal segmentation — handles semantic, instance, panoptic in one model
Masked attention prevents spurious correlations
Excellent on rare/minority classes via per-query prediction
weaknesses: Requires large dataset for full potential (>2000 images recommended)

ranked_models.name: UperNet (ConvNeXt-T backbone)
strengths: Pyramid pooling captures multi-scale aerial features
ConvNeXt modernises the CNN backbone with transformer-like design
weaknesses: Higher param count than SegFormer for similar performance
No global self-attention — still CNN-limited receptive field

ranked_models.name: DeepLabV3+ (ResNet-101 + ASPP)
strengths: Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling captures multi-scale features
Strong on dense prediction tasks (roads, buildings)
Good pretrained weights available
weaknesses: No global attention — misses cross-image flood patterns
Requires more training data than U-Net to excel

ranked_models.name: U-Net (ResNet-50 backbone)
strengths: Proven architecture for medical & aerial imagery
Works well with small datasets via skip connections
Fast inference
weaknesses: Struggles with long-range dependencies (flood spread patterns)
Weaker on imbalanced classes vs. transformer models

ranked_models.name: FCN (VGG-16 backbone)
strengths: Simple, well-understood architecture
Reasonable speed
weaknesses: Outdated — significantly outperformed by modern architectures
Very coarse segmentation for fine-grained classes
